site.cli.hint: Paste one of these into a terminal or a CI job to deploy to `{domain}`. Each deploy makes a new release, and earlier releases stay so you can roll back.
site.cli.keyHint: Both read your API key from `$SSH_KEY`, so set it first: `export SSH_KEY=sshost_…`

site.cli.zipTitle: Deploy a zip you already have
site.cli.zipHint: Put your zip's path after `file=@`. Its files go to the root of the site, and if they are all in one folder, they are taken out of it.
site.cli.folderTitle: Zip a folder and deploy it in one command
site.cli.folderHint: Sends the zip while it is made, so nothing is written to your disk. Change `dist` to your build folder.

site.visibility.title: Visibility
site.visibility.privateHint: Visitors must enter the passcode before this site shows them anything, and its pages stay out of shared caches and search engines. Set {date} by {name}.
site.visibility.publicHint: Anyone with the link can see this site. Set a passcode to keep it private, such as for a report or an unannounced product.
site.visibility.storedHint: The passcode is stored hashed and cannot be shown again, so keep a copy with the link. Visitors who entered it stay in for {duration}, unless you change or remove it.
site.visibility.removeConfirm: Remove the passcode from {domain}? Anyone with the link can then see the site.
site.visibility.changed: Changed the passcode for {domain}. Visitors who used the old one must enter the new one.
site.visibility.madePrivate: {domain} is now private. Visitors must enter the passcode.
site.visibility.madePublic: {domain} is public again. Anyone with the link can see it.
site.https.title: HTTPS
site.https.outsideHint: HTTPS ends in front of this server, such as at a reverse proxy or a Cloudflare Tunnel, so its certificates are managed there. HSTS below still works on answers that came over HTTPS; to end HTTPS in this server instead, see **HTTPS** in the menu.
site.https.selfSignedNote: Browsers warn about a self-signed certificate. It suits Cloudflare's “Full” mode and private networks.
site.https.plainHttp: None. This site answers over plain HTTP only.
site.https.nextAttempt: This server tries again after {date}, or now if you select **Renew now**. For Let's Encrypt, the domain's DNS must point at this server, and port 80 must reach it.
site.https.option.cloudflareOrigin: Cloudflare Origin certificate (for a site Cloudflare proxies)
site.https.option.uploaded: The certificate uploaded for this site
site.https.automaticHint: Automatic uses a shared certificate that covers this site, uploaded under **HTTPS** in the menu. Without one, it uses this server's default, which is Let's Encrypt unless set otherwise.
site.https.hsts: HSTS: tell browsers to use only HTTPS, for 1 year
site.https.hstsHint: Turn on HSTS only when HTTPS works reliably. A browser that has seen it refuses plain HTTP for this domain for 1 year, even if you turn it off here.
site.https.removeConfirm: Remove the certificate uploaded for {domain}? The site goes back to an automatic certificate.
site.https.upload: Upload a certificate for this site
site.https.uploadHint: Paste the certificate as PEM, then any intermediate certificates, and its private key, which is stored encrypted and never shown again. For a certificate that covers many sites, such as `*.example.com`, upload it once under **HTTPS** in the menu instead.
site.https.savedCertificateSoon: Saved the HTTPS settings for {domain}. If it needs a new certificate, it gets one within 1 minute.
site.https.removed: Removed the uploaded certificate. {domain} uses an automatic certificate again.
site.https.renewing: Asked for a new certificate for {domain}. Reload the page in a few seconds to see it.
site.proxy.title: Proxy routes
site.proxy.hint: Forward paths on this site to other servers, such as Docker containers. Requests pass the site's passcode and functions first, so they protect what a route forwards.
site.proxy.unsetEnvironment.one: This server has no environment variable `{names}`. A route whose target uses it answers 502 until it is set, and a request header that uses it is sent empty.
site.proxy.unsetEnvironment.other: This server lacks the environment variables `{names}`. A route whose target uses one answers 502 until it is set, and a request header that uses one is sent empty.
site.proxy.serverHint: Server-wide routes that apply to this site, set under **Proxy** in the menu. Where this site has its own route at the same path, its own route is used.
site.proxy.memberHint: Only administrators can change proxy routes, because a route makes this server send requests wherever it points.
site.proxy.memberEmpty: This site has no proxy routes. Only administrators can add them, because a route makes this server send requests wherever it points.
site.proxy.serverOn: The server-wide route at {path} applies to {domain} again.
site.proxy.serverOff: The server-wide route at {path} is off for {domain}.
site.proxy.removed: Removed the proxy route at {path} from {domain}.
site.route.sitesHint: `*` for every site, `*.apps.example.com` for every site under that domain, or one domain; separate several with commas. A site's own route at the same path is used instead, and each site can turn this route off.
site.route.pathHint: The path matches whole segments, ignoring case: `/api` covers `/api/users` but not `/apis`, and `/` covers everything. The longest matching path is used, and the target can read an environment variable, such as `${env:ORDERS_URL}`.
site.route.enabledHint: When off, the route is kept, but its paths go to the site's files.
site.route.stripPathHint: On: `/api/users` goes to the target as `/users`. Off: as `/api/users`.
site.route.webSocketsHint: Forwards WebSocket connections, over HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2. When off, they are refused.
site.route.crossSiteWebSocketsHint: Lets pages on other sites open them. The visitor's cookies are sent too, so leave this off unless the target checks `Origin` itself.
site.route.streamingHint: For server-sent events, long polling and large downloads. This server never compresses or buffers them.
site.route.grpcWebHint: For a gRPC server without gRPC-Web. A browser's gRPC-Web calls go to it as gRPC over HTTP/2, and the answers come back as gRPC-Web.
site.route.filesFirstHint: Serves the site's file when there is one at the path, and forwards only when there is not.
site.route.forwardedHeadersHint: Sends `X-Forwarded-For`, `-Proto`, `-Host` and, when the path is removed, `-Prefix`. Any that the visitor sent are always dropped.
site.route.keepHostHint: For a target that tells sites apart by name. When off, the `Host` header names the target.
site.route.rewriteRedirectsHint: A redirect to the target's own address is changed to the same place on this site.
site.route.acceptAnyCertificateHint: For an `https://` target with a self-signed certificate, on a network you trust. Anyone between this server and the target could read the traffic.
site.route.settingsHint: Auto uses HTTP/2 when an `https://` target offers it, and HTTP/1.1 otherwise; gRPC and translated gRPC-Web always use HTTP/2. The timeout is how long the target may send nothing, an idle WebSocket included.
site.route.cookies: Cookies the target sets belong to
site.route.cookiesHint: A parent domain shares the cookies with its other subdomains, for sites that share a sign-in. Cookies named like this server's own (`ssh.*`) are never passed on, in either direction.
site.route.requestHeadersHint: One `Name: value` per line, set on every request to the target; `Name:` alone removes that header. Read keys and passwords from `${env:…}`, so they are never stored in the site's settings.
site.route.removeServerConfirm: Remove the server-wide route at {path} for {sites}? Its paths go back to each site's own files and routes.
site.route.removeConfirm: Remove the proxy route at {path}? Its paths go back to the site's files.
site.route.bodyLimitError: Largest request body: enter a number of megabytes above 0, with a dot for decimals, such as 0.5 or 10. Or leave it empty.
site.headers.title: Header rules
site.headers.hint: Set response headers on the paths that match a pattern, such as to turn off caching or add a security header. By default, HTML gets `no-cache` and everything else gets `public, max-age={seconds}`.
site.headers.examplesLabel: Add an example, then edit it:
site.headers.example.noCacheJsonHint: For data files that change on every deploy but keep their names. The browser checks for a new copy each time.
site.headers.example.fingerprintedHint: Safe only when the file name changes with its content, as in `app.a1b2c3.js`.
site.headers.example.noStoreHint: Stronger than `no-cache`: the browser and proxies write nothing to disk.
site.headers.example.securityHint: Good defaults for a site that does not embed other sites and is not embedded by them.
site.headers.example.corsHint: Lets other sites fetch these files, such as fonts or data.
site.headers.example.feedHint: For a file that is rebuilt often and read often.
site.headers.helpTitle: How to write a header rule
site.headers.help.rule: A line that starts with `/` begins a rule. The indented `Name: value` lines under it are the headers it sets.
site.headers.help.comment: `#` starts a comment. Blank lines are ignored.
site.headers.help.pattern: In a pattern, `*` matches anything except `/`, `**` matches across `/`, and `?` matches one character. Matching ignores case.
site.headers.help.file: A rule matches either the requested URL or the file that answered it, so `/index.html` also covers `/`.
site.headers.help.order: Every matching rule applies, from top to bottom. When two set the same header, the later one is used, and rules here run after those that came with the release.
site.headers.help.noCache: `no-cache` means “check for a new copy every time”, not “never store”. ETags still work, so unchanged content costs only a `304`; use `no-store` when nothing may be kept.
site.headers.help.reserved: You cannot set the headers this server controls: `Content-Length`, `Transfer-Encoding`, `Connection`, `Content-Encoding`, `Set-Cookie`, `X-Content-Type-Options` and the other transport headers.
site.headers.fromRelease: The live release brought these in a `_headers` file. They run before the rules above, so where both set the same header, the rule above is used.
site.redirects.title: Redirects and rewrites
site.redirects.hint: A **redirect** (`301`, `302`, `303`, `307`, `308`) sends the visitor to another address, and the address bar changes. A **rewrite** (`200` or `404`) answers with another file at the same address.
site.redirects.examplesLabel: Add an example, then edit it:
site.redirects.example.movedHint: `301` tells browsers and search engines that the move is permanent.
site.redirects.example.sectionHint: `:1` stands for what the `*` matched, so `/blog/hello` goes to `/articles/hello`.
site.redirects.example.otherSiteHint: `**` matches across slashes, so the rest of the path is kept. `302` means the move is temporary.
site.redirects.example.folder: Serve one page for a whole folder
site.redirects.example.folderHint: A rewrite: the address stays the same and another file answers. For a single-page app at `/app`.
site.redirects.example.retireHint: Answers 404 with your own page, instead of acting as if the address still works.
site.redirects.example.force: Apply even where a file exists
site.redirects.example.forceHint: The `!` makes the rule apply even when the site has a file at that path.
site.redirects.help.line: One rule per line: where it comes from, where it goes, and the status. The status is optional; without one, it is `301`.
site.redirects.help.pattern: Patterns use the same `*`, `**` and `?` as header rules. In the address a rule goes to, `:1` to `:9` stand for what each wildcard matched, in order, and `:splat` is another name for `:1`.
site.redirects.help.first: The **first** rule that matches answers the request, so put specific rules above broad ones. Rules here are tried before those that came with the release.
site.redirects.help.files: A rule **does not apply where a file exists**: if the site has a file at the requested path, that file is served. This stops a broad rule such as `/**` from catching your stylesheets; put `!` after the status to apply it anyway.
site.redirects.help.where: A redirect can go to a path on this site or to a full `https://` address; a rewrite must go to a path on this site. The visitor's query string is kept.
site.redirects.help.loop: A rewrite goes straight to the files, so one rewrite never starts another, and rules cannot loop.
site.redirects.help.cache: Browsers keep a `301` for a long time. Header rules apply to redirects too, so a matching header rule with `Cache-Control: no-store` stops browsers from keeping a permanent redirect.
site.redirects.help.index: You rarely need to rewrite every path to `index.html`: paths with no file already fall back to it.
site.redirects.fromRelease: The live release brought these in a `_redirects` file. They are tried after the rules above.
site.functions.title: Functions
site.functions.hint: C# code that answers requests on this site before its files: public static methods with attributes such as `[HttpGet("/path")]`, in `.cs` files or LINQPad `.linq` queries. Upload them here or in a zip's `_functions/` folder; a deploy keeps them, and rolling back asks which ones to run.
site.functions.none: The live release runs no functions.
site.functions.removeConfirm: Stop running functions on {domain}? Earlier releases keep theirs.
site.functions.memberHint: Only administrators can upload functions, because they run as code inside this server.
site.functions.removed: {domain} no longer runs any functions. Earlier releases keep theirs.
site.variables.title: Variables
site.variables.hint: Named values the site's pages and functions read, declared with defaults in a `_variables.json` file at the root of the zip. A value set here stays through deploys and rollbacks; public ones reach the browser through `/_host/site.js`, and functions see all of them, secrets included.
site.variables.missing.one: A required variable is empty: `{names}`. Set it below.
site.variables.missing.other: Required variables are empty: `{names}`. Set them below.
site.variables.unsetEnvironment.one: A value here reads an environment variable that this server does not have, so it is empty: `{names}`.
site.variables.unsetEnvironment.other: Values here read environment variables that this server does not have, so they are empty: `{names}`.
site.variables.column.name: Name
site.variables.useDefaultConfirm: Remove the value set here for {name}? It goes back to the release's default, or to no value if the release has none.
site.variables.environmentNotSet: `{name}` is not set on this server
site.variables.administratorsOnlyTitle: Only an administrator can set, change or remove a secret, or a value that reads this server's environment.
site.variables.none: There are no variables yet. Declare them in a `_variables.json` file in the zip, or add one below.
site.variables.addHint: For something the release does not declare. Names are case-sensitive.
site.variables.addMemberHint: Only an administrator can set secrets, or values that read this server's environment with `${env:…}`.
site.variables.name: Name
site.variables.nameTitle: Letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter or an underscore
site.variables.public: Public: sent to the browser in `/_host/site.js`
site.variables.secret: Secret: stored encrypted and never shown again
site.variables.secretKept: {name} was not changed. An empty box keeps a secret's value.
site.variables.noOwnValue: {domain} has no value of its own for {name}.
site.variables.noValue: {name} no longer has a value, because the release gives it no default.
site.ai.title: AI
site.ai.hint: Lets the site chat through one of this server's AI providers: functions use `IAiChat`, and pages use `site.ai.chat` in `/_host/site.js`, for visitors allowed here or by the site's `[AiAccess]` hook. The provider's key stays on this server, and the model and system prompt set here apply to every chat.
site.ai.providerDeleted: The AI provider this site used was deleted, so the site has no AI. Choose another below.
site.ai.noProviders: There are no AI providers yet. [Add one under AI](aiUrl), then choose it here.
site.ai.systemPromptPlaceholder: You answer questions about this site, briefly and kindly.
site.ai.systemPromptHint: Sent before every conversation, up to {size} KB. A page or a function can add instructions after it, but cannot remove it.
site.ai.hookHint: Not used now: the site's `[AiAccess]` hook, `{hook}`, decides which visitors may chat while the live functions have it. This setting applies again if a deploy removes the hook.
site.ai.visitorWarning.one: Every visitor's question is billed to the provider's key, and anyone who can open the site can ask. Each IP address may ask {count} question a minute here, which slows a stranger down but does not limit the bill. Leave this off to keep chat to the site's functions, which decide who may ask.
site.ai.visitorWarning.other: Every visitor's question is billed to the provider's key, and anyone who can open the site can ask. Each IP address may ask {count} questions a minute here, which slows a stranger down but does not limit the bill. Leave this off to keep chat to the site's functions, which decide who may ask.
site.ai.visitorWarningNoLimit: Every visitor's question is billed to the provider's key, and anyone who can open the site can ask. This server sets no limit per IP address (`SiteHosting:AiVisitorRequestsPerMinute` is 0), so nothing slows a stranger down. Leave this off to keep chat to the site's functions, which decide who may ask.
site.ai.removeConfirm: Remove the AI settings from {domain}? Its functions and pages can then no longer chat.
site.ai.memberHook: The site's `[AiAccess]` hook, `{hook}`, decides which visitors' pages may chat.
site.ai.memberVisitors: Visitors are allowed, so pages on the site can chat.
site.ai.memberNoVisitors: Visitors are not allowed, so only the site's functions can chat.
site.ai.memberHint: Only administrators can change the AI settings, because they spend the provider's key.
site.ai.memberNone: This site has no AI. Only administrators can set it up, because it spends a provider's key.
site.ai.snippetHint: `site.ai.enabled` says whether this page may chat. The promise resolves with the whole answer, the model and the tokens it used.
site.ai.savedHook: {domain} now chats through {provider}. Its `[AiAccess]` hook, {hook}, decides which visitors may use it.
site.ai.savedVisitors: {domain} now chats through {provider}, and every visitor can use it.
site.ai.savedFunctions: {domain} now chats through {provider}, for its functions only.
site.realtime.title: Realtime
site.realtime.hint: Sends events from this server to the pages open on this site, which listen with `site.realtime.on` from `/_host/site.js` and can join groups. Functions publish through `IRealtime`, and scripts and CI jobs through the API.
site.realtime.noPages: No page was connected when this page loaded.
site.realtime.pages.one: {pages} page was connected when this page loaded, in {groups}.
site.realtime.pages.other: {pages} pages were connected when this page loaded, in {groups}.
site.realtime.codeTitle: Code: listen from a page, and tell every open page
site.realtime.listenHint: This server sends `site.deployed` itself when a deploy, a rollback or new functions go live. The first `on` connects, and a lost connection comes back by itself; a handler gets the event's payload, then `{ event, group }`.
site.realtime.publishLabel: Tell every open page, from a script or a CI job
site.realtime.publishHint: Add `"payload"` with any JSON the pages need, and `"group"`, `"user"` or `"connection"` to reach fewer of them. The answer says how many connections it was sent to.
site.releases.title: Releases
site.releases.hint: Earlier releases stay on disk, so you can roll back at once.
site.releases.downloadTitle: A zip of this release, with its rules and variable declarations, ready to deploy again
site.branding.title: Visitor screens
site.branding.hint: The passcode, not-found and error screens visitors may see on this site. They use the server's branding unless you change it here; whatever you leave as it is follows the server's.
site.branding.removeConfirm: Use the server's branding on {domain}'s visitor screens again? Its own name, logos and colours are removed.
site.branding.saved: Saved the branding of {domain}'s visitor screens.
site.branding.sameAsServer: Nothing differs from the server's branding, so {domain} uses it as it is.
site.branding.removed: {domain}'s visitor screens use the server's branding again.
site.rename.title: Change domain
site.rename.hint: Moves the site, with all its releases, rules and passcode, to another domain. {domain} stops answering at once and nothing redirects from it, so point DNS at this server first, and update any deploy scripts that name it.
site.rename.confirm: Move {domain} to the new domain? The old domain stops working at once.
site.rename.done: {from} is now {to}. {from} no longer serves anything.
site.rename.donePasscode: {from} is now {to}. {from} no longer serves anything, and visitors must enter the passcode again.
site.delete.title: Delete the site
site.delete.hint: This deletes every release and all of the site's files from disk. It cannot be undone.
site.delete.confirm: Delete {domain} and all of its releases? This cannot be undone.
site.delete.done: Deleted {domain} and all of its releases.
